title: Shortest paths without weights
summary: Use BFS distances and parent pointers to find the fewest-edges route.
hints: BFS already knows the distance: when you discover `v` from `u`, `dist[v] = dist[u] + 1`. Start with a `dist` slice of `len(g)` entries all set to `-1` (a loop does it); `-1` doubles as the 'not visited' marker, so you do not need a separate visited slice.
For `ShortestPath`, run the same BFS but also record `parent[v] = u` at the moment you discover `v`. You can stop early once `target` is discovered.

To rebuild the path, walk backwards from `target` following `parent` until you reach `start`, appending each vertex, then `slices.Reverse(path)`. Handle `start == target` (path is just `[start]`) and an unreachable target (return nil).
